name: Skywave Gateway · Reticulum HF Mesh Bridge
tag: Plans long-range off-grid radio links, from HF propagation to a Reticulum-to-LoRa bridge.

scenarios.title: Plan a regional HF link
scenarios.ask: Link two off-grid sites {dist} apart, mostly during the {tod}, at {power}.
steps: Propagation
At {dist}, near-vertical skywave (NVIS) fits best: signals go up and bounce down over the region.
Frequency
Suggested about {=tod} MHz for {tod} use, below the usual maximum usable frequency.
Antenna
A half-wave dipole of about {=round(143 / tod, 1)} m, mounted low at about {=round(0.15 * 300 / tod)} m for NVIS.
Link budget
At {power}, estimated {=round(min(99, 70 + power / 5))}% link reliability in typical conditions.
followups: Yes, for transmitting on HF in almost every country. The app asks for your license class and only suggests frequencies it allows.
For NVIS, a low dipole sends more energy straight up, which is what covers a region without a skip zone.

scenarios.title: Bridge a LoRa mesh over HF
scenarios.ask: Bridge our {nodes}-node LoRa mesh to a distant site over HF. We send about {msgs} messages an hour.
steps: Bridge
Set up a Reticulum gateway that joins the local LoRa mesh and the HF link.
Traffic
{msgs} messages an hour at about 200 bytes each is {=round(msgs * 1600 / bps, 1)} seconds of HF airtime.
Scheduler
Batched messages so the HF radio transmits in short bursts.
Monitor
Added a status page showing queued, sent and delivered messages for {nodes} nodes.
followups: Yes. Reticulum is designed to work over very slow links, so a {bps} modem is enough for short text messages.
What about encryption on amateur bands?
Many countries limit encryption on amateur bands. The app flags your settings so you can stay within your license rules.

scenarios.title: Survey noise with an SDR
scenarios.ask: Scan {bands} bands at our site for {hours} and find the quietest frequencies.
steps: SDR workbench
Scanned {bands} band(s) for {hours}, logging noise every 10 seconds.
Analyzer
Found a repeating noise spike, likely from a nearby power supply.
Ranker
Ranked channels by noise at each hour of the day.
Planner
Suggested a primary and backup channel for each band.
followups: How do I find the noise source?
Turn off circuits one at a time while the workbench watches. The noise drop shows which one it is.
No. Listening needs no transmit license in most places.
